finalText:
I allocated the new dock and monitor stock, gave every line that is still waiting a promise date, and sent each affected customer one notice. The one exception is O-5205 (C-525), which is on risk hold, so I left it alone.

**Allocated**
- **Laptop docks (P-DOC):** O-5201 (2), O-5202 L2, O-5204 (2), O-5207 L1, O-5209 (2), O-5210, O-5211 and O-5215.
- **Monitors (P-MON):** O-5202 L1, O-5203 (2), O-5207 L2, O-5208 (2) and O-5212.

**Still waiting, with promise dates**
- **O-5206 (ship-complete):** both lines are promised for 2026-08-14. The dock is covered by PO-95 (ETA 08-14), and the USB-C hub by PO-90 (ETA 08-06). The order gets the later date. It could not be allocated because the hub has no stock.
- **O-5213 (2 docks):** 2026-08-14, from PO-95.
- **O-5214 (1 monitor):** 2026-08-19, from PO-97.

**Policy update PU-12 and one mistake of mine**
- PU-12 (in force since 2026-07-01) puts orders placed 14 or more days before allocation at the head of the queue, oldest first, whatever the tier. I first ranked by tier alone. The reviewer blocked the O-5208 allocation, so I allocated O-5203 first.
- Before that I had already allocated O-5209 (a dock order) ahead of the older O-5201, and that cannot be undone. It made no difference to the outcome, because both orders ended up allocated.

**PO-91 and PO-93 also arrived**
- During the run, PO-91 (4 docks) and PO-93 (3 monitors) were also marked received. I counted that stock as on hand.
- Without it, O-5201 (a dock order) and O-5208 (a monitor order) would have been left waiting. That would have been the wrong call, since O-5201 is aged under PU-12 and O-5208 is gold tier.
- It also means the dock and monitor promise dates above come from the remaining in-transit POs only.

**Notices**
- Fourteen notices went out: 11 allocated, plus O-5206, O-5213 and O-5214 with their promise dates.
